lessons.title: సోమవారం to ఆదివారం — Telugu's week, with a twist on Sunday
lessons.headword: సోమవారం మంగళవారం బుధవారం గురువారం శుక్రవారం శనివారం ఆదివారం
lessons.gloss: the seven weekdays — Sanskritic like Hindi, but Sunday means "the FIRST day," not "Sun's day"

segments.text: Like Kannada, Telugu's week runs on Sanskrit deity-names — but its Sunday breaks the "planet" pattern entirely, in a way even Kannada's doesn't.

blocks.title: The word, taken apart - The pattern: [deity] + వారం, "day"

utterances: Telugu: సోమవారం (Somavāram). deity/planet: Moon (Soma). day: Monday.
Telugu: మంగళవారం (Maṅgaḷavāram). deity/planet: Mars (Maṅgala). day: Tuesday.
Telugu: బుధవారం (Budhavāram). deity/planet: Mercury (Budha). day: Wednesday.
Telugu: గురువారం (Guruvāram). deity/planet: Jupiter (Guru/Bṛhaspati). day: Thursday.
Telugu: శుక్రవారం (Śukravāram). deity/planet: Venus (Śukra). day: Friday.
Telugu: శనివారం (Śanivāram). deity/planet: Saturn (Śani). day: Saturday.
Telugu: ఆదివారం (Ādivāram). deity/planet: — not a planet at all. day: Sunday.

blocks.title: Why it's said this way: Be honest: Sunday isn't a planet-name here

segments.text: Five days match the familiar planet-deity pattern — but ఆదివారం (Ādivāram) doesn't name the Sun at all. ఆది (ādi) is Sanskrit for "the beginning, the first." So Telugu's Sunday literally means "the first day" — a positional name, like Arabic's numbered weekdays, sitting right next to six planet-names that don't work that way. Even within one single week, a language can mix completely different naming strategies.

segments.instruction: "Somavāram, Maṅgaḷavāram, Budhavāram, Guruvāram, Śukravāram, Śanivāram" — Monday through Saturday
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "Somavāram, Maṅgaḷavāram, Budhavāram, Guruvāram, Śukravāram, Śanivāram" — Monday through Saturday]

segments.instruction: the odd one — "Ādivāram" — not a planet, "the first day"
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the odd one — "Ādivāram" — not a planet, "the first day"]

segments.instruction: the parallel — like Arabic's numbered days, one Telugu day is positional too
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the parallel — like Arabic's numbered days, one Telugu day is positional too]

segments.text: What does ఆదివారం literally mean, and is it a planet-name? ("The first day" — ādi "beginning" — not a planet-name, unlike the other six.) What ending do the other six Telugu weekdays share? (‑వారం -vāram, Sanskrit "day," each paired with a planet-deity.)
